item: The findings of the coordinator's check of #1292: a failed call is not in the browse report, the latency summary builds its rows outside the lock record takes, the durable search-timing lines stop repeating their static text, and three paths gained a test
key_paths: src/monitoring/latency.py; src/monitoring/search_timing.py; tests/test_latency_attribution.py; tests/test_search_timing_browse.py; tests/test_kpi_k2_attribution.py; docs/product/RELEASE_0.4_GATE.md; docs/ledger/SHIPPED_LOG.md
summary: #1292 was merged before the coordinator's check of it ended, so its findings ride the next PR. The browse report's method text now says what the code does: a call that failed is not in it (the route latency log counts those) and a call for a fixed set of ids is not timed. latency.summary() built every route's row (three sorts of a window of up to 512) while holding the lock record() takes on the event-loop thread; it now copies each route under the lock and builds the rows after releasing it (300 routes with full windows: about 38 ms of row-building outside the lock, the copies holding it about 4 ms in the measurement here), with a test that the rows are built unlocked and one that a request recorded meanwhile does not change a row already copied, both failing on the old code. N3: the two durable search-timing logs wrote the same method and caveat words on every line and nothing reads them back (the report carries them once), so a line is now the measurement only, as the coordinator's note of 03:49 asked: a browse line went from 1,937 to 196 bytes (the log at its 5,000-line cap from 9.7 to 0.98 MB) and a text line from 1,043 to 193 bytes (5.2 to 0.97 MB), and the cut of 5,250 lines, which rewrites the whole file on the request thread every 250th append, from 39.9 to 2.5 ms for a browse log and from 13.8 to 2.6 ms for a text log (medians of seven cuts, warm cache, the module's own writer and cut). The in-process window keeps the whole record, the caller's dict is never cut, a log written before holds both shapes until the cuts drop the older one, and the durable summary says so; the schema string stays because no key a reader uses moves. The log docstring quotes the sizes and times before and after, the page-size bound says what it protects, and the cache-off count phase and the tie between UNLOCK_ROUTES and the unlock router's own routes are tested. Ledger text: the #1292 row says K2's formula is unchanged (not its value) and names both of its lessons, the gate's row D sentence no longer attributes to Q117 a rule it does not state, and row A says a later judging attempt, an own one or an imported one, makes the verdict read measured. Five small findings of the same check ride along: the passphrase is out of what ANY phase's exception says in the report, the state file and the log (the error log keeps a traceback's tail in app_errors.jsonl, which a bundle carries), a child that cannot be started leaves no empty install directory, a comment and a docstring no longer overclaim, and the number, tunables and preload rules of the allocator reading are now also checked against a real glibc child, 26 shapes, where fakes alone had pinned them.
